Jonas / Marissa — thanks for the draft. A few technical clarifications and attachments I'm adding:

1) Telemetry & retention (redwood_sg_privacy_snapshot.pdf)
- Ingestion traces: 90 days (raw), operational aggregates: 365 days
- Flagged-output events (policy triggers): retained 730 days for audit + 30-day high-fidelity window for debugging
- Access logs: 1 year (rotated, encrypted at rest)

2) Detection and classification
- Misuse signals come from: model-heuristic detectors (pattern + blacklists), user-behavior anomalies (rate spikes / prompt provenance), and ML-based reranking that flags disallowed content.
- Severity buckets: HIGH (immediate policy violation — auto-block + incident), MEDIUM (requires human review within 24 hours), LOW (observational telemetry, weekly digest)
- Sample rule: repeated prompt commonality + high toxicity score => MEDIUM (escalates to reviewer)

3) Escalation & SLAs (incident_playbook.pdf)
- On detection (HIGH): Pager to on-call SRE + Security lead within 15 minutes; containment action within 60 minutes; remediation plan within 24 hours.
- MEDIUM: Triage queue, acknowledge within 4 hours, review within 24 hours.

4) Log redaction process (log_sample_redacted.jsonl)
- PII tokenization + irreversible hashing for identifiers; free-text snippets truncated to 128 chars and redacted if pattern-match hits; full request/response withheld unless explicitly approved under NDA.

5) Attestation: attaching SOC2_Type2_Report_2026 (exec summary) — we can provide full report under NDA.

I'll attach the files here for review. Marissa — if you can confirm the program-level contacts and the one-line intro for the cover note I'll update and send.

— Soojin
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
